verdict.rationale: Self-hosting is a fair question for a SaaS MCP directory, gateway, and hosting platform, so the axis applies. However, every piece of evidence describes Glama-hosted services: the hosted inspector, deploying servers "to Glama", and a Gateway that every MCP call "flows through". Nothing documents a way to run Glama's own core product on user infrastructure. Using mcp-proxy to tunnel local MCP servers to Glama's inspector is an adjacent feature, not self-hosting Glama.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product
